# E022 -- Barbican

## Metadata
- **Brand:** Barbican Centre
- **Industry:** Arts / Culture (multi-art-form venue)
- **Year:** Not dated (estimated mid-2010s based on design style)
- **Region:** London, UK
- **Source file:** barbican-brand-guidelines.pdf
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13, 14-20, 27-32, 38-45
- **Total pages:** 56 (internal page numbering goes to 137 due to spread numbering)

## Brand Strategy
- Multi-art-form identity system: the brand must unify Theatre, Art Gallery, Curve Gallery, Film, Music, and corporate Barbican communications.
- Each art form has its own visual sub-identity within a shared typographic and grid framework.
- The identity is defined by "a strong typographic style and expression" with principles based on "function, format and purpose."
- Contact point: printdesign@barbican.org.uk centralises brand asset distribution and approvals.

## Logo
- Circular logo mark, always supplied as a full circle and set to bleed off the page edge.
- Logo artwork supplied with crop marks for alignment; crop marks must be removed in final artwork.
- Exclusion zone defined to protect clarity and visual integrity.
- Lock-up system: logo + text information positioned on the Barbican grid, with defined placements for different formats (A5, A4, A3).
- Special case lock-up for co-branding with resident companies or promoters -- preferably black or reversed white on dark background.

## Typography
- **Primary typeface:** Futura (Scangraphic font library version, from scangraphic-fonts.com).
- Described as "at the heart of the Barbican identity" -- clean, distinctive, legible, with contemporary and classical qualities.
- Key weights: Futura Bold is most used across all art forms. Futura SB Bold and Futura SH Bold both acceptable.
- Full weight range available for creative expression.
- **Typography rules:**
  - Always ranged left (flush left, ragged right).
  - Never set sentences solely in capitals; use sentence case.
  - Leading set tighter than default.
  - Tracking usually less than default for body text.
  - Careful kerning required for headlines.
- **Art-form-specific typographic treatments:**
  - Art Gallery: Futura Bold Italic at 9-degree angle, with highlighting and outlining treatments.
  - Art Gallery signature: stacked "barbican artgallery" with precise alignment rules (leading at 75% of character size).
  - Theatre (bite): dynamic signature incorporating "dance, music, theatre" with programme year in italic numerals.

## Color
- Not extensively detailed in text-extracted pages; the document references "full-colour examples" in later pages.
- Art form sub-identities appear to use distinct colour treatments (Theatre described as "colourful and dynamic").
- Primary palette appears to be black/white with art-form-specific accent colours.

## Graphics / Illustration
- No standalone illustration system; the identity is purely typographic and photographic.
- Each art form has its own visual character:
  - Theatre: colourful, dynamic imagery inspired by performance energy.
  - Art Gallery: 9-degree italic angle as a consistent graphic device.
  - Curve Gallery: its own differentiation within the Art Gallery identity, "contemporary character."

## Photography
- Theatre identity uses "colourful and dynamic imagery inspired by the energy of performances."
- Image libraries maintained per art form, accessible via printdesign@barbican.org.uk.
- Photography appears to be the primary visual differentiator between art forms within the shared typographic framework.

## Applications
- Comprehensive grid system: formats divided into equal vertical units, providing framework for logo, lock-up, and content positioning.
- Six-column grid for marketing literature, with flexibility for combining text and images.
- Grid sets accommodate multiple formats (A5, A4, A3 and beyond).
- Design examples section covers practical application across all art forms.

## Tone of Voice
- Not covered in sampled pages; the guidelines are exclusively focused on visual identity.
- The writing style within the guidelines themselves is precise, instructional, and design-literate.

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- Art-form-specific sub-identities within a unified framework is a sophisticated approach -- Theatre, Art, Film, Music each get their own section with dedicated typographic and visual treatments.
- The Art Gallery's 9-degree italic angle is a distinctive and unusual brand device.
- The Scangraphic-specific version of Futura is specified (not just "Futura") -- this level of font foundry specificity is uncommon.
- The grid system is remarkably detailed and central to the identity, serving as the connective tissue across all art forms.
- Centralised asset distribution through a single email contact reflects a tightly controlled brand governance model.

## Quality Score
4 / 5 -- Highly systematic identity guide with excellent typographic depth, detailed grid specifications, and a clever multi-art-form architecture. The sub-identity system for each art form is well structured. Loses a point for limited colour specification detail in extractable text and no tone-of-voice section. The internal page numbering system (spread-based) is slightly confusing relative to actual PDF pages.
